cases.title: A hold on the wrong side: never called done; points at the key at the start of the pair

rubric.reason: Turn 3 does not call the 1–1.4 s pair done ("isn't there yet"), names the key at 1 s as "the one that needs the hold" in line with the check's wrong_side verdict, and does not fix it.

Turn 3 says what is still off and where, with real names and times (the hold is on the key at 1.4 s, and the 1.4–1.8 s and 1.8–2.2 s pairs still fade), then hands the work back with "Hold all three of Blink's pairs and say done" without offering to do it.

Every name and time (Blink, Cut, Seal, Dot 1 at 0.5 s, Opacity, pairs at 1/1.4/1.8/2.2 s, frames at 1.2/1.6/2 s) appears in the snapshot or check results, and "partly see-through" follows from the eased state of those pairs.
Turn 3 calls the 1–1.4 s pair 'isn't there yet' and points at the start key: 'the key that has to hold is the one at 1 s, at the start of the pair', without fixing it.

Turn 3 names what is off and where (Blink's Opacity 1–1.4 s held on the wrong key; 1.4–1.8 s and 1.8–2.2 s still fade), then ends 'Fix those three and say done again', with no offer to fix and no step-by-step fix.

Every name and time used (Blink, Cut, Seal, Dot 1 at 0.5 s, Opacity, 1/1.4/1.8/2.2 s, 1.2/1.6/2 s) appears in or follows from the snapshot and check results, including the wrong-side hold at 1.4 s implied by the 'wrong_side' verdict.

In turn 3 the check returned wrong_side for Blink › Opacity 1–1.4 s; the mentor says it "isn't done", points at "the key at 1 s, at the start of the pair" as the one that needs to hold, and doesn't fix it.

Turn 3 names what is off and where (Blink's Opacity 1–1.4 s on the wrong key, and the 1.4–1.8 s and 1.8–2.2 s pairs still fading) and hands it back with "Hold the keys at 1 s, 1.4 s and 1.8 s, then say done." It doesn't fix anything or offer to.

Every name and time the mentor uses appears in the tool results: Blink, Opacity, Cut at 3 s, Dot 1 at 0.5 s, Seal as a precomp, the pair times 1/1.4/1.8/2.2 s and the check frame times 1.6 s and 2 s. The "half see-through" remarks follow from the eased 100↔0 pairs in the snapshot.
